title: Choose the visual world for CGV Experience
question: The roll assigned Countdown Leader. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Palette stays pinned to your brief: dark ground, CGV red accent.

options.label: Countdown Leader
options.thesis: Every experience is a reel on the projector: the site counts you down to your slot.
materials: printed edge codes and frame numbers
options.viewport: Hero photo framed as one projected frame between sprocket rails, a countdown ring ticking to 'Book a slot', service frames running down the strip.
options.risk: Film-strip motifs turn into costume if sprockets decorate instead of carrying sequence; every strip must hold real slots, steps or services.

raised.raise: Booking runs down one axis: each step is the next frame on the same reel, never a new screen.
Depth only from stacked flat planes of film and paper; no glows, no neon halos, no gradients.
One grease-pencil circle marks the single thing that matters on each view (the chosen slot, the total).
Every time slot shows its value and its trend: spots left, not just open or closed.

options.label: Showtime Board
options.lineage: cinema lobby showtime boards and ticket stubs
options.thesis: Services listed like tonight's screenings; booking prints you a ticket stub.
options.viewport: A lobby board listing Escape Room, Photo Booth and Combo with next free times, hero photo beside it.
options.risk: The most familiar cinema-site arrangement; where most runs in this category land.

options.label: Street-Fashion Spread
options.thesis: The photobooth crowd as a packed magazine spread, every offer labelled by hand with its price.
options.viewport: Cut-out friends from the booth photos shingled across the hero with hand price tags on each service.
options.case: Strong audience identification with Hanoi photobooth culture; loses on clarity for the escape room and the booking flow.
options.risk: Needs real cut-out mattes the source photos cannot provide cleanly.

options.label: Versailles Bosquet Vistas
options.thesis: Axial vistas opening onto hidden garden theaters.
options.viewport: A palace-axis vista with services as bosquets.
options.risk: No connection to a cinema night out.
options.case: Loses both axes: the audience does not identify with formal gardens.
options.kept: Booking as one continuous axis of frames.

options.label: Łowicz Papercut
options.thesis: Depth by pasted flat colour layers.
options.risk: Folk craft fights the cinema brand.
options.kept: Depth from stacked flat planes, never glow.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.viewport: A doodled diagram of the four booking steps.
options.risk: Cream-paper default; reads childish for a night out.
options.kept: One annotation marks the thing that matters.

options.label: Night-flight Six-pack
options.kept: Every slot shows value and trend.

options.label: Tropicália Sleeve
options.thesis: Mismatched-scale cut-outs in a painted jungle.
options.risk: Tropical palette breaks the pinned dark-and-red brief.
options.kept: Courage in scale contrast between headline and detail.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean dark booking site: hero banner, three service cards, steps, contact form.
canonCard.viewport: Hero banner with headline and Book now, three equal service cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every booking template by design.
